rule_objections: The rule's 'up to four modules deep' is stated in terms of modules, but include struct/sig, a functor argument and a constrained module hide contents from the tool without being modules; the rule should say so.
findings: Items inside 'include struct ... end' and 'include sig ... end' blocks are not extracted; in container_intf.ml that hides about 54 definitions (module types, types, vals) in one 380-line stretch, in hashtbl_intf.ml about 39. This is the normal shape of Jane Street's _intf files. Not in KNOWN_GAPS.
Module aliases (module List = List0) and the contents of a module with a 'with type' constraint or a functor parameter signature are also missed.
What is found is right: 313 symbols, no spurious; operators such as ( + ) and ( +. ) are named by the operator; externals are functions; module types are interface.
Destructive substitutions ('type t := ...') were not counted as expected definitions.
not_done: Expected sets from a regex over val/module/type/external/exception/let lines with comment lines skipped, reconciled against the symbols; I did not read all 2,166 lines, and the symbols the regex missed (names on the line after val) were treated as correct after sampling.
